summary.en: The nineteenth ruler of Goguryeo (r. 391–413), whose campaigns against Baekje, the Wa and peoples to the north made Goguryeo the dominant power of Northeast Asia. His deeds are recorded on the stele his son raised in 414.
summary.zh: 高句丽第十九代君主（391—413年在位），征伐百济、倭及北方诸族，使高句丽成为东北亚强国。其功业记载于其子414年所立的石碑上。

label.en: Campaign against Baekje on the Han River
Sends army to aid Silla against the Wa
label.zh: 出兵救援新罗、击退倭军

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)

note: Campaign sites are known mainly from the stele inscription and are approximate.

summary.en: A descendant of the Geumgwan Gaya royal house who became Silla's leading general. He commanded Silla armies in the conquest of Baekje (660) and Goguryeo (668) and is honoured as the architect of unification.
summary.zh: 金官伽倻王族后裔，后成为新罗首席将领。他指挥新罗军队参与灭百济（660年）与灭高句丽（668年）的战争，被尊为三国统一的功臣。

label.en: Named supreme commander as Silla–Tang forces take Pyongyang; ill, he stays in Gyeongju
label.zh: 受命为大总管，因病留守庆州，联军攻陷平壤

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)

note: Birthplace and Nangbi fortress locations are traditional identifications.

summary.en: A semi-legendary prince who served as regent for Empress Suiko. Tradition credits him with the Seventeen-article constitution, the twelve-rank cap system, embassies to Sui China and the founding of Hōryū-ji.
summary.zh: 半传说性的皇子，曾为推古天皇摄政。传统上认为他制定了冠位十二阶与十七条宪法，派遣遣隋使，并创建法隆寺。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Buddhist Monuments in the Horyu-ji Area

note: Most achievements attributed to him come from the Nihon Shoki and later hagiography; their historicity is disputed.

summary.en: A lady-in-waiting to Empress Shōshi at the Heian court and author of The Tale of Genji, as well as a diary and poetry collection that offer a vivid picture of aristocratic life around 1000.
summary.zh: 平安时代侍奉中宫彰子的女官，《源氏物语》的作者，另著有日记与和歌集，生动展现了公元1000年前后的贵族生活。

label.en: Returns to the capital and marries

label.zh: 最后见于记载，约卒于此年

sources.title: Murasaki Shikibu, Murasaki Shikibu nikki (Diary, c. 1010)
Richard Bowring, Murasaki Shikibu: The Tale of Genji (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2004)

note: Birth and death years are estimates (c. 973–c. 1014; some scholars propose 978 or a death as late as 1031). Wikidata's death year of 1100 is not supported by the scholarship.

summary.en: A maritime magnate from Songak who served the warlord Gung Ye before overthrowing him in 918 and founding Goryeo. He absorbed Silla and defeated Later Baekje, reuniting the peninsula in 936.
summary.zh: 出身松岳海上豪族，曾效力于弓裔，918年推翻弓裔建立高丽。他先后接纳新罗归降、击败后百济，于936年重新统一朝鲜半岛。

label.zh: 一利川之战击败后百济

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Taejo of Goryeo (Wang Geon)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)

summary.en: Exiled to Izu as a boy after his father's defeat, he raised the Minamoto against the Taira in 1180, won the Genpei War through his commanders, and founded the first warrior government at Kamakura.
summary.zh: 其父战败后，少年源赖朝被流放伊豆。1180年他举兵讨伐平氏，通过部将赢得源平合战，并在镰仓建立了日本第一个武家政权。

sources.title: Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)

summary.en: A ruthless and innovative warlord from Owari who seized Kyoto in 1568, deposed the last Ashikaga shogun in 1573 and subdued much of central Japan, before being forced to suicide by his vassal Akechi Mitsuhide at Honnō-ji.
summary.zh: 出身尾张、行事果决而富于革新的战国大名。1568年进入京都，1573年放逐末代足利将军，平定日本中部大部分地区，后在本能寺遭家臣明智光秀背叛而自尽。

sources.title: Jeroen P. Lamers, Japonius Tyrannus: The Japanese Warlord Oda Nobunaga Reconsidered (Hotei, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)

summary.en: Born a commoner, he rose in Nobunaga's service, avenged him in 1582 and completed the military unification of Japan in 1590. He froze social classes, surveyed the land and launched the disastrous invasions of Korea.
summary.zh: 出身平民，在织田信长麾下崛起，1582年为信长复仇，1590年完成日本统一。他推行刀狩与太阁检地、固定身份等级，并发动了失败的侵朝战争。

label.zh: 山崎之战击败明智光秀

label.en: Directs the Korean invasion from Nagoya, Hizen
label.zh: 坐镇肥前名护屋指挥侵朝

sources.title: Mary Elizabeth Berry, Hideyoshi (Harvard University Press, 1982)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)

summary.en: A patient survivor of the Sengoku wars who moved his base to Edo in 1590, won at Sekigahara in 1600 and became shogun in 1603. After destroying the Toyotomi at Osaka he left a dynasty that ruled until 1867.
summary.zh: 在战国乱世中隐忍求存，1590年移封江户，1600年赢得关原之战，1603年就任将军。在大坂之役消灭丰臣氏后，他所建立的德川家族统治日本直至1867年。

label.en: Becomes shogun; Edo seat of government
label.zh: 就任将军，以江户为政治中心

label.en: Rules as retired shogun from Sunpu
label.zh: 以大御所身份坐镇骏府

sources.title: Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)

summary.en: The fourth king of Joseon (r. 1418–1450). He sponsored scholars of the Hall of Worthies, advances in astronomy, agriculture and music, northern frontier expansion and, above all, the creation of the Korean alphabet, Hangul.
summary.zh: 朝鲜王朝第四代国王（1418—1450年在位）。他扶持集贤殿学者，推动天文、农学与音乐的发展，开拓北方疆域，最重要的成就是创制了朝鲜文字“训民正音”。

label.en: Six Garrisons on the Tumen River established

sources.title: Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)

summary.en: Commander of the Joseon navy during the Imjin War, celebrated for his turtle ships and an unbroken record of victories that cut Japanese supply lines. He was killed by a bullet in his last battle at Noryang.
summary.zh: 壬辰战争期间的朝鲜水军统帅，以龟船和屡战屡胜著称，切断了日军的海上补给线。在最后一战露梁海战中中弹殉国。

label.zh: 出任全罗左水使，驻丽水

sources.title: Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Invasion: Japan's Korean War 1592–98 (Cassell, 2002)

summary.en: Emperor from 1867 to 1912, in whose name the Meiji Restoration was carried out. During his reign Japan adopted a constitution, industrialised, and defeated China and Russia to become an imperial power.
summary.zh: 1867至1912年在位的日本天皇，明治维新以其名义推行。在其治下，日本颁布宪法、实现工业化，并先后击败清朝与俄国，跻身帝国主义列强。

sources.title: Donald Keene, Emperor of Japan: Meiji and His World, 1852–1912 (Columbia University Press, 2002)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)

summary.en: A low-ranking samurai from Tosa who left his domain to work for national reform. He founded a trading company in Nagasaki, brokered the Satsuma–Chōshū alliance in 1866 and proposed the peaceful return of power to the emperor, but was assassinated in Kyoto weeks later.
summary.zh: 出身土佐藩的下级武士，脱藩投身维新事业。他在长崎创办龟山社中，1866年促成萨长同盟，并提出将政权和平奉还天皇的构想，数周后在京都遇刺身亡。

label.en: Founds the Kameyama Shachū in Nagasaki
Brokers the Satchō Alliance in Kyoto
Assassinated at the Ōmiya inn, Kyoto

sources.title: Marius B. Jansen, Sakamoto Ryōma and the Meiji Restoration (Princeton University Press, 1961)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)

summary.en: A samurai's son from Iga, Bashō moved to Edo and turned haikai linked verse into a serious art valuing sabi and lightness. His travel journals, above all Oku no Hosomichi from the journey of 1689, blend prose and haiku; he died on the road in Osaka.
summary.zh: 芭蕉出身伊贺的武士家庭，迁居江户后把俳谐连句提升为崇尚“寂”与“轻”的严肃艺术。他的纪行文，尤其是记述1689年旅行的《奥之细道》，融散文与俳句于一体；他病逝于旅途中的大阪。

label.en: Settles in the Bashō hut at Fukagawa
Oku no Hosomichi journey reaches Hiraizumi
label.zh: 奥之细道之旅抵达平泉

summary.en: Born at Ojukheon in Gangneung, Shin Saimdang was admired for her paintings of plants and insects, her landscapes and her calligraphy. Mother of the Neo-Confucian scholar Yi I (Yulgok), she was later idealised as a model mother, and since 2009 her portrait has appeared on the 50,000-won note.
summary.zh: 申师任堂生于江陵乌竹轩，以草虫图、山水画和书法著称。她是理学家李珥（栗谷）的母亲，后世被奉为贤母良妻的典范，2009年起其肖像印于韩国五万韩元纸币上。

label.en: Gives birth to Yi I at Ojukheon

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Korean Culture: 신사임당 (Shin Saimdang)

summary.en: A monk from Shikoku who studied Esoteric Buddhism in Tang Chang'an under Huiguo and founded the Shingon school on his return. A celebrated calligrapher, poet and engineer, he founded the monastery on Mount Kōya and is the focus of the 88-temple Shikoku pilgrimage.
summary.zh: 出身四国的僧人，在唐朝长安师从惠果学习密教，回国后开创真言宗。他是著名的书法家、诗人和工程营造者，开创了高野山，也是四国八十八所朝圣的信仰中心。

label.zh: 生于赞岐屏风浦（今善通寺）

label.en: Ship drifts to the Fujian coast
Studies with Huiguo at Qinglong temple, Chang'an
label.zh: 在长安青龙寺师从惠果

sources.title: Yoshito S. Hakeda, Kūkai: Major Works (Columbia University Press, 1972)

role.en: Court lady and author of The Pillow Book

summary.en: Daughter of the poet Kiyohara no Motosuke, she served Empress Teishi from about 993 until the empress died in 1000, and wrote The Pillow Book, a witty miscellany of court life. Her real name is unknown and her later life is obscure.
summary.zh: 歌人清原元辅之女，约自993年起侍奉皇后定子，直到定子于1000年去世，著有描写宫廷生活、机智灵动的随笔集《枕草子》。她的真名不详，晚年生活也鲜为人知。

label.en: Enters Empress Teishi's service at the Heian palace
label.zh: 入平安宫侍奉皇后定子

label.en: Pillow Book circulating in the capital
Said to live in retirement at Tsukinowa, Higashiyama

sources.title: Ivan Morris (trans.), The Pillow Book of Sei Shōnagon (1967)

note: Birth and death years are approximate; the Tsukinowa retirement is a tradition.

role.en: Regent and leader of the Fujiwara clan

summary.en: The most powerful of the Fujiwara regents. By marrying four daughters to emperors he became grandfather of three, dominated the court from 995 to 1027, and patronised Murasaki Shikibu through his daughter Empress Shōshi. His diary Midō kanpakuki survives in his own hand.
summary.zh: 藤原摄关中权势最盛者。他把四个女儿嫁给天皇，成为三位天皇的外祖父，从995年到1027年主宰朝政；通过女儿中宫彰子，他也是紫式部的庇护者。其亲笔日记《御堂关白记》留存至今。

label.en: Pilgrimage to Mount Kinpu; buries sutras
Regent for his grandson Go-Ichijō at the Tsuchimikado mansion
label.zh: 在土御门殿任外孙后一条天皇的摄政

label.en: "Full moon" poem at the Tsuchimikado banquet
label.zh: 于土御门殿宴上咏“望月”之歌

sources.title: Francine Hérail (trans.), Notes journalières de Fujiwara no Michinaga (Droz, 1987–1991)
Fujiwara no Sanesuke, Shōyūki (diary), entry for Kannin 2 (1018)

role.en: Samurai general of the Genpei War

summary.en: Half-brother of Minamoto no Yoritomo, he won the decisive battles of the Genpei War at Ichi-no-Tani, Yashima and Dan-no-ura. Distrusted by Yoritomo, he fled to Hiraizumi, where he was betrayed and died in 1189, becoming Japan's archetypal tragic hero.
summary.zh: 源赖朝的异母弟，在一之谷、屋岛和坛之浦赢得源平合战的决定性胜利。他遭赖朝猜忌，逃往平泉，1189年被出卖而死，成为日本悲剧英雄的典型。

label.en: Under Fujiwara no Hidehira at Hiraizumi
Joins Yoritomo at the Kise river

sources.title: Helen Craig McCullough (trans.), Yoshitsune: A Fifteenth-Century Japanese Chronicle (Stanford, 1966)

note: His childhood at Kurama and early years are known mainly from later legend (Gikeiki).

summary.en: Daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa and wife of Minamoto no Yoritomo. After his death she became a nun but, with her brother Yoshitoki, held real power in the Kamakura shogunate; her speech to the vassals in 1221 rallied them against Retired Emperor Go-Toba in the Jōkyū War.
summary.zh: 北条时政之女，源赖朝之妻。赖朝死后她出家为尼，却与弟弟北条义时一起掌握镰仓幕府实权；1221年承久之乱时，她对御家人的演说使他们团结起来对抗后鸟羽上皇。

label.en: Shelters at Izusan shrine during Yoritomo's rising
label.zh: 赖朝起兵时避难于伊豆山

label.en: After Sanetomo's murder, governs as "nun shogun"
label.zh: 源实朝遇刺后，以“尼将军”身份主政
号召御家人对抗后鸟羽上皇

sources.title: Hitomi Tonomura, "Women and Inheritance in Japan's Early Warrior Society", Comparative Studies in Society and History 32:3 (1990)

role.en: Emperor of Japan, leader of the Kenmu Restoration
role.zh: 日本天皇，建武新政的主导者

summary.en: The 96th emperor, who plotted against the Kamakura shogunate, was exiled to Oki, escaped and overthrew it in 1333. His attempt at direct imperial rule collapsed when Ashikaga Takauji rebelled, and he founded the Southern Court at Yoshino.
summary.zh: 第九十六代天皇。他密谋倒幕，被流放隐岐后脱逃，于1333年推翻镰仓幕府。足利尊氏反叛后，他的天皇亲政尝试失败，遂在吉野建立南朝。

label.en: Escapes to Mount Senjō in Hōki
Establishes the Southern Court at Yoshino

sources.title: H. Paul Varley, Imperial Restoration in Medieval Japan (1971)

summary.en: A Kamakura general who switched sides in 1333 to help Go-Daigo destroy the Hōjō, then turned on the emperor, installed a rival line of the Northern Court and became shogun in 1338, founding the Muromachi shogunate.
summary.zh: 镰仓幕府的将领，1333年倒戈协助后醍醐天皇消灭北条氏，随后又与天皇反目，扶立北朝天皇，1338年就任征夷大将军，开创室町幕府。

label.en: Takes Rokuhara in Kyoto for Go-Daigo
label.zh: 为后醍醐攻下京都六波罗

label.en: Retakes Kamakura and breaks with the court

label.zh: 在京都受封征夷大将军

sources.title: Thomas D. Conlan, State of War: The Violent Order of Fourteenth-Century Japan (Michigan, 2003)

summary.en: Shogun from 1368 to 1394, he reunited the Northern and Southern Courts in 1392, curbed the great provincial lords, opened official trade with Ming China as "King of Japan" and built the Golden Pavilion, presiding over the flowering of Noh and Kitayama culture.
summary.zh: 1368年至1394年任将军。他于1392年实现南北朝合一，压制强大的守护大名，以“日本国王”名义开启对明勘合贸易，并营建金阁，主导了能乐和北山文化的繁荣。

label.en: Builds the Palace of Flowers at Muromachi
Builds the Kitayama villa and Golden Pavilion

sources.title: John W. Hall and Toyoda Takeshi (eds.), Japan in the Muromachi Age (University of California Press, 1977)

summary.en: Japan's most celebrated ink painter. Trained at the Zen temple Shōkoku-ji, he settled under the Ōuchi lords in Yamaguchi, travelled to Ming China in 1468–69 and developed a bold landscape style seen in his Long Landscape Scroll and View of Amanohashidate.
summary.zh: 日本最负盛名的水墨画家。他在禅寺相国寺修行，后投奔山口的大内氏，1468—1469年随使团入明，形成雄健的山水画风，代表作有《四季山水图卷》（山水长卷）和《天桥立图》。

label.en: Monk and painter at Shōkoku-ji, Kyoto
label.zh: 在京都相国寺为僧习画

label.en: Settles at Yamaguchi under the Ōuchi
Lands at Ningbo with the Japanese mission
Paints the Long Landscape Scroll at Unkoku-an

sources.title: Yukio Lippit, "Of Modes and Manners in Japanese Ink Painting: Sesshū's Splashed Ink Landscape of 1495", The Art Bulletin 94:1 (2012)
Kyoto National Museum, Sesshū: Master of Ink and Brush (exhibition catalogue, 2002)

note: The date and place of his death are uncertain; the Amanohashidate view is usually dated c. 1501–06.

role.en: Unifier and first king of the Ryukyu Kingdom

summary.en: A lord of Sashiki in southern Okinawa who overthrew the king of Chūzan in 1406, conquered Hokuzan and, in 1429, Nanzan, uniting Okinawa as the Ryukyu Kingdom with Shuri as its capital and expanding its tribute trade with Ming China.
summary.zh: 冲绳南部的佐敷按司，1406年推翻中山王，先后攻灭北山和南山（1429年），把冲绳统一为以首里为都城的琉球王国，并扩大了对明朝的朝贡贸易。

sources.title: George H. Kerr, Okinawa: The History of an Island People (Tuttle, 1958; rev. 2000)
Gregory Smits, Visions of Ryukyu: Identity and Ideology in Early-Modern Thought and Politics (University of Hawaii Press, 1999)

note: Dates follow the later Ryukyuan official histories and are not confirmed by contemporary sources.

role.en: Ainu chief and leader of the 1669 revolt
role.zh: 阿伊努首领，1669年起义领袖

summary.en: Chief of the Menashikur Ainu on the Shibuchari river in southern Hokkaido, he led the largest Ainu uprising against the Matsumae domain in 1669 and was killed at a peace banquet. He is remembered as a symbol of Ainu resistance, with a statue at Shizunai.
summary.zh: 北海道南部静内河流域麦那西库尔阿伊努人的首领，1669年领导了反抗松前藩的最大规模阿伊努起义，在议和宴会上被杀。他被视为阿伊努抵抗的象征，静内立有他的雕像。

label.en: His army is stopped at Kunnui
Killed at the Pipok peace banquet

sources.title: Brett L. Walker, The Conquest of Ainu Lands: Ecology and Culture in Japanese Expansion, 1590–1800 (University of California Press, 2001)
Shinhidaka Town: Shakushain memorial and statue (Shizunai)

note: His birth year is unknown (Wikidata gives 1606); events are known mostly from Matsumae accounts.

summary.en: An Edo artist who used some thirty names and moved house about ninety times in a career of seventy years. His Hokusai Manga sketchbooks and the landscape series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, including the Great Wave, influenced European Impressionism.
summary.zh: 江户画家，七十年的创作生涯中用过约三十个画号，搬家约九十次。他的《北斋漫画》和包括《神奈川冲浪里》在内的风景组画《富岳三十六景》影响了欧洲印象派。

label.en: Debut as a pupil of Katsukawa Shunshō
label.zh: 入胜川春章门下首次发表作品

label.en: First Hokusai Manga published in Nagoya
label.zh: 《北斋漫画》初编在名古屋出版

label.en: Paints a giant Daruma in Nagoya
label.zh: 在名古屋绘制巨幅达摩像

label.en: Paints temple ceilings at Obuse, Shinano
label.zh: 在信浓小布施绘制寺院天井画

sources.title: Timothy Clark, Hokusai: Beyond the Great Wave (2017)

role.en: Satsuma samurai and Meiji Restoration leader
role.zh: 萨摩藩武士，明治维新领导人

summary.en: A lower samurai of Satsuma who survived two island exiles to lead the alliance that overthrew the shogunate and negotiated the peaceful surrender of Edo in 1868. He left the government in 1873 and died leading the Satsuma Rebellion in 1877.
summary.zh: 萨摩藩的下级武士，两度被流放海岛后东山再起，领导推翻幕府的同盟，1868年谈判实现江户无血开城。1873年他辞官下野，1877年在领导西南战争时战死。

label.en: In Edo as aide to Shimazu Nariakira
Negotiates the surrender of Edo with Katsu Kaishū
label.zh: 与胜海舟谈判江户开城

sources.title: Mark Ravina, The Last Samurai: The Life and Battles of Saigō Takamori (2004)

role.en: Statesman, first prime minister of Japan
role.zh: 政治家，日本首任内阁总理大臣

summary.en: A Chōshū samurai who studied in London in 1863, drafted the Meiji Constitution, served four times as prime minister and negotiated the Treaty of Shimonoseki. As first Resident-General of Korea (1905–09) he oversaw the protectorate and was assassinated at Harbin by An Jung-geun.
summary.zh: 长州藩武士，1863年留学伦敦，起草明治宪法，四度出任首相，并主持签订《马关条约》。他作为首任韩国统监（1905—1909年）推行保护国统治，在哈尔滨被安重根刺杀。

label.en: Studies in London with the Chōshū Five
In Washington with the Iwakura Mission
label.zh: 随岩仓使节团在华盛顿

label.en: Studies constitutions in Berlin and Vienna
label.zh: 在柏林、维也纳考察宪法
出任首任内阁总理大臣

label.en: Treaty of Shimonoseki with Li Hongzhang
label.zh: 与李鸿章签订《马关条约》

sources.title: Kazuhiro Takii, Itō Hirobumi: Japan's First Prime Minister and Father of the Meiji Constitution (Routledge, 2014)

role.en: Educator and writer, founder of Keio
role.zh: 教育家、思想家，庆应义塾创办人

summary.en: A low-ranking samurai who learned Dutch and then English, sailed to America in 1860 and Europe in 1862, and explained Western civilisation to Japanese readers in best-selling books such as An Encouragement of Learning. He founded the school that became Keio University.
summary.zh: 出身下级武士，先学兰学后学英语，1860年赴美、1862年赴欧，以《劝学篇》等畅销书向日本读者介绍西方文明，创办了后来的庆应义塾大学。

label.en: Born at the Nakatsu domain warehouse in Osaka
label.zh: 生于大阪中津藩藏屋敷

label.en: Studies at Ogata Kōan's Tekijuku, Osaka
label.zh: 入大阪绪方洪庵的适塾

label.en: Opens a Dutch school in Edo (Tsukiji)
label.zh: 在江户筑地开设兰学塾

label.en: San Francisco aboard the Kanrin Maru

label.zh: 随幕府使节团游历欧洲

sources.title: Eiichi Kiyooka (trans.), The Autobiography of Yukichi Fukuzawa (Columbia University Press, 1966)

summary.en: Emperor through militarism, war, defeat and recovery. Regent from 1921 and emperor from 1926, he sanctioned the wars in China and the Pacific, decided on surrender in 1945, renounced his divinity in 1946 and reigned as a constitutional symbol until his death. His role in the war remains debated.
summary.zh: 经历军国主义、战争、战败和复兴的天皇。1921年任摄政，1926年即位，他批准了侵华战争和太平洋战争，1945年决定投降，1946年宣布否定自身神格，此后作为宪法规定的象征在位直至去世。他在战争中的责任至今仍有争论。

label.en: Born at the Aoyama palace, Tokyo

label.zh: 以皇太子身份访问欧洲

label.en: State visit to the United States

sources.title: Herbert P. Bix, Hirohito and the Making of Modern Japan (HarperCollins, 2000)
Stephen S. Large, Emperor Hirohito and Shōwa Japan (Routledge, 1992)

role.en: Buddhist monk and philosopher of Silla

summary.en: Silla's most influential Buddhist thinker, author of some eighty works including commentaries read in China and Japan. According to legend he abandoned a journey to Tang China after an awakening, left monastic life, fathered the scholar Seol Chong, and spread Pure Land devotion among ordinary people.
summary.zh: 新罗最有影响的佛教思想家，著述约八十部，其中的注疏在中国和日本广为流传。据传说，他在赴唐途中顿悟而放弃西行，后来还俗，生下学者薛聪，并在平民中传播净土信仰。

label.en: Awakening on the road to the Tang, by legend near Dangju
label.zh: 传说在赴唐途中于党项津附近顿悟
在庆州与瑶石公主结合

sources.title: Robert E. Buswell Jr., Cultivating Original Enlightenment: Wonhyo's Exposition of the Vajrasamādhi-Sūtra (University of Hawaii Press, 2007)

note: Stops after 661 are approximate and partly legendary.

role.en: Maritime commander and trader of Silla
role.zh: 新罗海上军事首领、商人

summary.en: An islander who served in the Tang army, returned to found the Cheonghaejin garrison on Wando in 828, suppressed slave-raiding pirates and dominated trade between Silla, Tang China and Japan. Drawn into Silla court politics, he was assassinated.
summary.zh: 出身海岛，曾在唐军中服役，828年回国后在莞岛设立清海镇，打击掳卖人口的海盗，主导了新罗、唐朝与日本之间的贸易。后来卷入新罗宫廷政治而遇刺身亡。

label.en: Born on the southwestern islands (Wando area)
label.zh: 生于西南岛屿（今莞岛一带）

label.en: Officer in the Wuning army, Xuzhou
His troops win at Dalgubeol for Kim U-jing (Sinmu)
label.zh: 其军在达句伐为金祐征（神武王）取胜

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Edwin O. Reischauer, Ennin's Travels in T'ang China (1955)

note: Birth year is a modern estimate. The Samguk sagi dates his death to 846; the Japanese Shoku Nihon kōki implies 841.

summary.en: A civil official who topped the state examination in 983, Gang Gam-chan opposed surrender during the Khitan invasion of 1010 and, at the age of seventy, commanded the Goryeo army that annihilated the Liao invaders at Gwiju in 1019.
summary.zh: 文臣出身，983年科举状元。1010年契丹入侵时他反对投降；七十岁时统率高丽军，于1019年在龟州全歼辽朝入侵军。

label.zh: 生于衿川（今首尔落星垈）

label.en: Tops the state examination in Kaesong
label.zh: 在开京科举及第为状元

label.en: Urges King Hyeonjong not to surrender

sources.title: Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Gang Gam-chan

role.en: General, founder of the Joseon dynasty
role.zh: 将领，朝鲜王朝开国君主

summary.en: A frontier general from the northeast who won fame against the Red Turbans and Japanese pirates, turned back from the Liaodong campaign at Wihwado in 1388, and founded Joseon in 1392, moving the capital to Hanyang (Seoul) in 1394.
summary.zh: 出身东北边疆的将领，因抗击红巾军和倭寇而成名，1388年在威化岛回军，1392年建立朝鲜王朝，1394年迁都汉阳（今首尔）。

label.en: Helps recapture Kaesong from the Red Turbans
label.zh: 协助从红巾军手中收复开京

label.en: Withdraws to Hamhung after the princes' strife

sources.title: Joseon wangjo sillok (Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty)
John B. Duncan, The Origins of the Chosŏn Dynasty (2000)

role.en: Inventor and engineer of the Joseon court

summary.en: Born a government slave in Dongnae, Jang Yeong-sil was promoted by King Sejong for his skill with instruments. He studied astronomical devices in Ming China and built the self-striking water clock (Jagyeongnu) of 1434 and other instruments, before falling from favour in 1442 when a royal palanquin he oversaw broke.
summary.zh: 出身东莱官奴，因善制器械受到世宗提拔。他曾赴明朝考察天文仪器，主持制造了1434年的自击漏等仪器；1442年因其监造的御辇损坏而失宠。

label.en: Born a government slave in Dongnae
Sent to Ming Beijing to study astronomical instruments
label.zh: 被派往明朝北京考察天文仪器

label.en: Builds the Okru clock in Heumgyeonggak
Dismissed after the royal palanquin breaks

sources.title: Joseph Needham et al., The Hall of Heavenly Records (1986)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Jang Yeong-sil

note: Birth year is unknown (c. 1390; Wikidata gives 1400). 1442 is his last appearance in the records, not a recorded date of death.

summary.en: Korea's most revered Neo-Confucian scholar. After a career in office he retired to Andong, founded the academy that became Dosan Seowon, debated the theory of principle and material force with Gi Dae-seung, and presented the Ten Diagrams of Sage Learning to King Seonjo. He appears on the 1,000-won note.
summary.zh: 朝鲜最受尊崇的性理学家。他在仕途之后退居安东，创办了后来的陶山书院，与奇大升展开“四端七情”理气之辩，并向宣祖进呈《圣学十图》。他的肖像印在一千韩元纸币上。

label.en: Passes the civil examination in Hanseong
Magistrate of Punggi; wins a royal charter for Baegundong academy
label.zh: 任丰基郡守，为白云洞书院请得赐额

label.en: Presents the Ten Diagrams of Sage Learning

sources.title: Michael C. Kalton (trans.), To Become a Sage: The Ten Diagrams on Sage Learning by Yi T'oegye (Columbia University Press, 1988)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies

note: He died in the 12th lunar month of 1570, which falls in January 1571 in the Gregorian calendar.

summary.en: A favourite of King Jeongjo who helped design Hwaseong Fortress and its crane. After Jeongjo's death he was exiled for eighteen years, mostly at Gangjin, for his family's links to Catholicism, and there wrote some 500 volumes on government, law and classics, including Mongmin simseo on the duties of a magistrate.
summary.zh: 正祖的宠臣，参与设计水原华城及其起重机。正祖死后，他因家族与天主教的关联被流放十八年，大部分时间在康津度过，在那里写下约五百卷有关政治、法律和经学的著作，其中包括论述地方官职责的《牧民心书》。

label.en: Designs the Hwaseong fortress and crane
Exiled to Janggi after the Catholic persecution

sources.title: Mark Setton, Chŏng Yagyong: Korea's Challenge to Orthodox Neo-Confucianism (SUNY Press, 1997)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Jeong Yak-yong

role.en: Leader of the Donghak Peasant Revolution

summary.en: A village teacher and Donghak leader known as "Green Bean General" for his small stature, he led the Gobu rising of 1894, took Jeonju, and in the autumn led peasant armies against Japanese troops until their defeat at Ugeumchi. Betrayed and captured, he was executed in Seoul.
summary.zh: 乡村塾师和东学接主，因身材矮小人称“绿豆将军”。1894年他领导古阜起义，攻占全州；秋天又率农民军抗击日军，直到在牛禁峙战败。他遭出卖被捕，在汉城被处死。

sources.title: George L. Kallander, Salvation through Dissent: Tonghak Heterodoxy and Early Modern Korea (University of Hawaii Press, 2013)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Jeon Bong-jun

summary.en: Chosen as Gojong's queen in 1866, she became the leading political force at court, opposing the regent Heungseon Daewongun, backing cautious reform and balancing China, Japan and Russia. She was murdered by Japanese agents in Gyeongbokgung in 1895 and posthumously named empress.
summary.zh: 1866年被选为高宗王妃，后来成为宫廷中的主要政治力量，与摄政兴宣大院君对立，支持稳健改革，并在中国、日本和俄国之间寻求平衡。1895年她在景福宫被日本人杀害，后被追封为皇后。

label.en: Flees the Imo mutiny to Janghowon
label.zh: 壬午军乱时出逃长湖院

label.en: Returns to the palace with Qing help

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword (1995)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Myeongseong Hwanghu

role.en: King of Joseon and first emperor of Korea
role.zh: 朝鲜国王，大韩帝国首位皇帝

summary.en: King from 1863, first under his father the Heungseon Daewongun's regency, Gojong presided over the opening of Korea, fled to the Russian legation after his queen's murder, proclaimed the Korean Empire in 1897, and was forced to abdicate by Japan in 1907 after sending secret envoys to The Hague. His funeral helped spark the March First Movement.
summary.zh: 高宗1863年即位，起初由其父兴宣大院君摄政。他经历了朝鲜开港，王妃被害后避入俄国公使馆，1897年宣布成立大韩帝国，1907年因密派使者赴海牙而被日本逼迫退位。他的葬礼成为三一运动的导火索之一。

label.en: Takes refuge in the Russian legation
Proclaims the Korean Empire at Hwangudan
label.zh: 在圜丘坛宣布建立大韩帝国

label.en: Forced to abdicate at Gyeongun palace

sources.title: Bruce Cumings, Korea's Place in the Sun: A Modern History (Norton, 1997)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Gojong

summary.en: A Catholic educator and righteous-army fighter from Hwanghae who assassinated Itō Hirobumi at Harbin in 1909. Executed at Lüshun in 1910, he left calligraphy and an unfinished Treatise on Peace in East Asia and is honoured as a national hero in both Koreas.
summary.zh: 黄海道出身的天主教徒、教育家和义兵战士，1909年在哈尔滨刺杀伊藤博文。1910年在旅顺被处决，留下书法作品和未完成的《东洋和平论》，在朝鲜半岛南北都被尊为民族英雄。

label.en: Runs the Samheung school at Jinnampo
label.zh: 在镇南浦创办三兴学校
在海参崴加入流亡者团体
在克拉斯基诺附近断指同盟
在哈尔滨击毙伊藤博文

sources.title: Franklin Rausch, "The Harbin Assassination and the Unfinished Essay", Korean Studies 36 (2012)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): An Jung-geun

role.en: Student activist of the March First Movement
role.zh: 三一运动中的学生运动者

summary.en: An Ewha school student who joined the March First demonstrations in Seoul, returned to her home village and organised the Aunae market protest of 1 April 1919, where her parents were killed. Imprisoned at Seodaemun, she kept protesting and died there at seventeen after torture.
summary.zh: 梨花学堂学生，参加汉城的三一示威后返回家乡，组织了1919年4月1日并川阿佤内市场的示威，她的父母在示威中遇害。她被关押在西大门监狱，坚持抗争，十七岁时在狱中受刑而死。

sources.title: Seodaemun Prison History Hall: Yu Gwan-sun
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Yu Gwan-sun

role.en: Independence leader, president of the Provisional Government
role.zh: 独立运动领袖，临时政府主席

summary.en: A Donghak fighter turned nationalist who led the Korean Provisional Government in China, organised the Hongkou Park bombing of 1932 and the Korean Liberation Army. Returning in 1945, he opposed separate elections in the south and was assassinated in Seoul in 1949.
summary.zh: 出身东学军的民族主义者，在中国领导大韩民国临时政府，策划了1932年虹口公园爆炸案并组建韩国光复军。1945年回国后，他反对南方单独选举，1949年在汉城遇刺身亡。

label.en: Kills a Japanese at Chihapo after the queen's murder
label.zh: 闵妃遇害后在鸱河浦杀死一名日本人

label.en: Joins the Provisional Government in Shanghai
Attends the North–South conference in Pyongyang
label.zh: 赴平壤出席南北协商会议

sources.title: Kim Gu, Baekbeom ilji (autobiography; trans. Jongsoo Lee, 2000)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Kim Gu

summary.en: A reformer imprisoned in the 1890s who earned a Princeton doctorate and spent decades lobbying for Korean independence in the United States. He became first president of the Republic of Korea in 1948, led it through the Korean War, ruled increasingly autocratically and was driven out by the April Revolution of 1960.
summary.zh: 1890年代因参与改革运动入狱，后获普林斯顿大学博士学位，在美国为朝鲜独立奔走数十年。1948年出任大韩民国首任总统，领导韩国度过朝鲜战争，统治日益专制，1960年被四一九革命赶下台。

label.zh: 获普林斯顿大学博士学位
以临时政府总统身份抵上海

sources.title: Robert T. Oliver, Syngman Rhee: The Man Behind the Myth (1954)

role.en: Founder and leader of North Korea
role.zh: 朝鲜民主主义人民共和国创建者和领导人

summary.en: A guerrilla commander in Manchuria in the 1930s who retreated to the Soviet Union in 1940 and returned with the Red Army in 1945. Leader of the DPRK from 1948 until his death, he launched the Korean War in 1950 and built a one-party state around the Juche ideology and a cult of his family.
summary.zh: 1930年代在中国东北领导游击队，1940年退入苏联，1945年随红军回国。1948年起领导朝鲜民主主义人民共和国直至去世，1950年发动朝鲜战争，并围绕“主体思想”和家族崇拜建立起一党制国家。

label.zh: 越过鸭绿江袭击普天堡

label.en: Retreats to a Soviet camp near Khabarovsk
label.zh: 退入哈巴罗夫斯克附近的苏联营地
在平壤宣布成立朝鲜民主主义人民共和国

label.en: Dies at a villa in the Myohyang mountains

sources.title: Dae-Sook Suh, Kim Il Sung: The North Korean Leader (Columbia University Press, 1988)

note: Details of his guerrilla years are overlaid by official North Korean mythology.

role.en: Military ruler and president of South Korea

summary.en: Trained in the Manchukuo and Japanese military academies, Park seized power in the May 16 coup of 1961 and ruled until 1979. He drove state-led export industrialisation, from expressways to the Pohang steelworks, while crushing dissent under the Yusin constitution of 1972. His intelligence chief shot him dead.
summary.zh: 朴正熙曾就读于伪满洲国和日本的军官学校，1961年发动五一六政变夺权，统治至1979年。他推行国家主导的出口工业化，从高速公路到浦项钢铁厂，同时以1972年的维新宪法压制异见。他被自己的情报部长枪杀。

label.en: Enters the Manchukuo military academy, Xinjing
label.zh: 入新京伪满洲国军官学校

sources.title: Byung-Kook Kim and Ezra F. Vogel (eds.), The Park Chung Hee Era (2011)

role.en: Democracy activist and president of South Korea
role.zh: 民主运动人士，韩国总统

summary.en: An opposition leader from South Jeolla who survived kidnapping, a death sentence and exile under military rule, was elected president in 1997, steered Korea through the Asian financial crisis, met Kim Jong-il in Pyongyang in 2000 and won the Nobel Peace Prize.
summary.zh: 出身全罗南道的在野领袖，在军人统治下历经绑架、死刑判决和流亡，1997年当选总统，带领韩国度过亚洲金融危机，2000年在平壤与金正日会晤，并获得诺贝尔和平奖。

label.en: Nearly defeats Park in the presidential election
label.zh: 在总统选举中险胜朴正熙未果

label.en: Kidnapped from a Tokyo hotel by Korean agents
label.zh: 在东京饭店被韩国特工绑架

label.en: Summit with Kim Jong-il in Pyongyang
Receives the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo
label.zh: 在奥斯陆领取诺贝尔和平奖

sources.title: Kim Dae-jung, Conscience in Action: The Autobiography of Kim Dae-jung (Palgrave Macmillan, 2019)
